_note: sprint is CLI-backed (./tools/sprint) and orchestrates sub-skills in reference/. A clean-context executor cannot run the CLI, so these cases are simulation-graded per skill-eval's Gotchas: grade whether the executor picks the right tier and the right sequence of steps (plan-before-code, approval gate, high-risk pipeline), not real CLI output.

evals.prompt: A user says: "sprint start: add a --json flag to the tkt ls command so it can print tickets as JSON." This adds a new option across a CLI file and its output path (coordinated, more than a cosmetic one-liner). Walk through what the sprint skill has you do.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as normal tier, runs `sprint start`, fills acceptance.md (criteria + test plan) and plan.md (approach), presents a brief, and waits for explicit user approval before writing any code. No orient/grill/impact-analysis unless a high-risk trigger appears.
expectations: Classifies the work as normal tier (not trivial — it adds coordinated behavior across a file/output path)
Creates acceptance.md and plan.md and presents a brief BEFORE writing implementation code
Waits for explicit user approval before coding, rather than jumping straight to implementation

evals.prompt: A user says: "Fix the typo in README.md — 'commmands' should be 'commands'." Walk through how the sprint skill handles this.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a trivial, single-line cosmetic change that is exempt from the sprint workflow: work directly and report verification, without creating a ticket or running sprint start.
expectations: Classifies the change as trivial (single-line / cosmetic typo fix)
Does not create a ticket or run the full sprint start planning flow
Makes the fix directly and reports verification

evals.prompt: A user says: "sprint start: change the login flow to accept OAuth tokens and store the refreshed session in a cookie." Walk through what the sprint skill has you do before coding.
evals.expected_output: Classifies this as high-risk (touches auth/sessions and security-sensitive behavior), and runs the full planning pipeline — orient (research.md), grill (resolve gray areas), impact analysis with required mitigation tests, and any human checkpoint — before implementation, gated on explicit approval.
expectations: Classifies the work as high-risk because it changes authentication/session behavior
Runs the high-risk pipeline (orient / grill / impact analysis) rather than the light normal-tier path
Requires mitigation tests for high risks and waits for approval before writing code

evals.prompt: A user says: "sprint start: move the board's inline <script> out of tools/sprint-check-app/app.html into a new tools/sprint-check-app/static/board.js." It touches every board user, so it is high-risk and you are in the orient (research) step. So far the research found that no source file imports app.html, and ran `git grep -n app.html -- tests/`, which printed one hit: `tests/board-spec.js:12: const html = fs.readFileSync(APP_HTML, 'utf8')`. Is the search for app.html's readers done? If not, say exactly what the research does next and what it records.
evals.expected_output: Says the reader search is not done: a search limited to importers and to tests/ is not enough. The research re-runs the grep repo-wide with no path or type filter, for the file name and the moved symbols, looks for readers that never import the file (tests in other languages, scripts that grep its text or fetch the page over HTTP), and lists and classifies every hit in research.md before moving on.
expectations: Says the search is not done because it was limited to importers and to tests/
Re-runs the grep over the whole repo with no path or type filter, for the file name and the moved or changed symbols
Names the kinds of non-import readers to look for: tests in other languages, and scripts that grep its text or fetch it over HTTP
Lists and classifies every hit (must change / still fine) in research.md before the research moves on
